body:
## Stack Context

FE-1433 sequences the Petrinaut integration from the proven Flue suspension and AI SDK seams. This branch is the ask suspend/return slice, stacked on FE-1436's durable transport; its panel-side counterpart is the FE-1448 host interactive-tool API in hashintel/hash (PR hashintel/hash#9249).

## What?

- `transport-aisdk` holds a `brunch_ask` open on the wire: awaiting client tool with a stable `toolCallId`, the harness's minted affordance output withheld
- the tool-result follow-up POST — previously refused wholesale — is admitted exactly when it carries the pending ask's correlated `{ answer }` submission
- `@brunch/core` gains the pure protocol: `pendingAskAffordanceId`, `decideAskReplyAdmission`, and the `AskSubmission` submitted-output contract
- the application's new `askReply` seam admits against durable Flue history before any dispatch, then resumes the conversation as a fresh user dispatch that the binding binds as the user-affordance reply
- opt-in inspection gains `ask-await`, `ask-reply-admitted`, `ask-reply-refused`

## Why?

FE-1449 requires provenance to settle at the wire boundary: a human answer travels tool-output-shaped but is not a machine tool result. Only the currently pending ask's correlated submission may become user evidence — stale/duplicate submissions get `409 ask_not_pending`, forged ids `409 ask_mismatch`, malformed submissions `400 invalid_ask_submission`, and machine-only follow-ups (mutation outputs, diagnostics) keep FE-1436's `422`. Concurrent duplicates collapse at the substrate via the `{conversationId}:ask:{toolCallId}` idempotency key.

Remaining for full FE-1449 acceptance: petrinaut-website registers the ask component through the FE-1448 `aiAssistant` API (hash-side branch); the implementation record names it.

## Verification

- `bun run smoke` — lint, fmt, typecheck, 163 tests
- `bun run build`
- wire contract tests for the translated ask part and each refusal class
- end-to-end run over the committed application route: the actual elicitor asks, the correlated answer resumes the same Flue conversation, a replayed duplicate is refused before dispatch

The provisional marker comes off after a full worked pass across three plugin targets (the FE-1397 precedent); the open strains (grade sources, support closure, temporal patterns, sweep-time concentration, the absence-locator envelope pressure) are first-class sections with owning tickets, not folded into the design.

This branch proves the first end-to-end question-and-reply path through the real application harness. It establishes that a question can pause a turn, persist, and bind the later answer correctly.

<details><summary>🏗️ Agent notes</summary>

This turns the ask seam into a working turn-suspension protocol: the tool mints a free-text affordance, parks it in the pending-affordance slot, returns it on the tool output part where its identity is durable, and terminates the turn — then the next user dispatch clears the slot and gets bound to that affordance by the harness itself, announced to the model as a signal rather than left to the model's memory. Because the pending question is never interpolated into the instructions, the instruction string cannot change between turns, which is what removes the wasted "instructions updated" wake turn the ticket-10 prototype hit once per question. The dev app is the proof: a chat UI plus an integration test that boots the real Flue runtime and the real Hono app in one process, drives them over a fetch shim with a scripted faux provider, and asserts in one shot that the reply binding reached the model, the affordance survived durably, no advisory wake appeared, and a second ask in the same batch was refused.

Deep-read record: `docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/notes/deep-read-fe-1389.md` (FE-1401 remediation sweep); hardening follow-ups filed as FE-1420.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

</details>

<details><summary>🏗️ Agent notes</summary>

Executes the FE-1400 bundle: the ten verified findings from the FE-1397 tie-off review, plus the cleanup tail, as small always-green commits. Each strengthened gate was red-proved — the violation it guards against was temporarily introduced and the gate watched go red — before restoring green.

**Docs truth:** the AGENTS.md triage one-liner now matches the triage doc's state/label mapping.

**Test integrity:** build-artifact witnesses are now strings unique to the guarded modules (`createAgentRouter`/`sqlite` both matched bootstrap code regardless of what bundled); the first-statement check reuses the shared directive pattern instead of a literal compare; the workspace walker's source/test partition is total (nested `src/test/` files no longer escape every invariant); the CI-gate check parses the workflow so commented-out or `if: false` gates read as absent; known-gaps predicates require an explicit `closes-gap: <id>` citation in a real test instead of `existsSync` on a guessed path — a stub can't close a gap, a differently-named real closure can. FWIW the citation-token design earned its keep immediately: the first draft accepted any prose mention of the gap id, and a doc comment in this branch's own new test closed a gap.

**Dev app:** the conversation store's default path anchors to the module (`db-path.ts`) instead of the launch directory, with tests for cwd-independence and the set-but-empty env override (which would have opened an anonymous temp database).

**Baseline runner:** the hand-rolled HTTP client is gone in favor of `@anthropic-ai/sdk` (network-error retries, retry-after, cache-token usage in the totals); truncation survives continuation stitching and is reported with the `--continue-final` escape hatch; fence matching tolerates the info-string forms real runs produce, and a delivered run that yields no extractable artifact — or an ambiguous multi-block one — says so loudly. The post-review pass also added an explicit SDK timeout (the doubled retry budget tripped the SDK's 10-minute non-streaming guard), no-clobber guards for fresh/`--resume` runs, and seam-exact stitching.

**Cleanup tail:** assets serve via a `/assets/*` wildcard and hono's MIME table (nested paths now work); CI builds once (root build inside `bun test`'s artifact suite, exercising every package's build script) and caches bun installs; the root build filter is `@brunch/*`; the runner's parallel `expertMessages` array and dead checkpoint field are gone; the boundary suite derives its topology pin from the spec's §12.2 block and its physical-resolution probes from the tree.

Two review findings deliberately not taken: swapping the hand-rolled asset handler for hono's `serveStatic` middleware (the strict dotfile/extension refusal semantics are pinned by tests and the ticket asked for framework routing + MIME table, both done), and de-obfuscating the composed `MODEL_KEY_NAME` pattern (an exclusion list for pattern-defining files has its own silent-failure mode; the composition predates this branch and is documented in place).

<details><summary>🏗️ Agent notes</summary>

Discharges the ratification condition on the generic IR definition (`ir-design.md`, Layer A): speculative payload type systems drafted for Gherkin (thin) and BPMN/process-mining (mid, the kernel spec's named third target), checked property-by-property alongside CPS (Layer B) and the assurance plugin from spec canon.

**Amended:** `ir-design.md` —
- All five MUST properties survive; property 2 generalized from statement granularity to **evidence granularity** (log-derived `external-lookup` captures have no user statement), property 3 restated operatively (its bite is proportional to domain–format distance; the enforceable content is IR-legitimacy of unconsumed kinds + the honest loss report).
- Symbolic name references promoted MAY → SHOULD (all four designs use them); the objective-kind pattern generalized to completion-anchor kinds; motif annotations demoted to a named escape hatch (zero uptake); **source-regime** promoted from Layer B to a Layer-A MAY pattern for process-shaped domains.

Review found checks that could pass while failing to protect the behavior they claimed to cover. This branch makes those checks and the development app report those failures instead of quietly accepting them.

<details><summary>🏗️ Agent notes</summary>

FE-1399: Make the CI gates and dev app fail loudly where review found they fail silently

The five verified findings from the FE-1361 review sweep:

- Agent-module detection is statement-anchored (shared in test/workspace.ts,
  unit-tested), so a comment mentioning 'use agent' no longer turns a file
  into an agent module — while a misplaced or comment-trailed directive is
  still detected and failed loudly.
- workspacePackages() derives its groups from the root manifest's workspaces
  globs; an unknown group, unreadable glob shape, or missing directory now
  throws instead of passing every boundary invariant vacuously.
- toolName() takes the Operation union instead of string, so a misspelled
  operation is a compile error; a @ts-expect-error test pins the narrowing.
- The dev app's mount path derives from GherkinElicitor.agentName, and a new
  boundary test forbids a pinned identity being duplicated as a string
  literal outside its agent module.
- The production /assets/:file route serves everything the client build can
  emit — bytes, not UTF-8; case-folded extensions; content-type map failing
  open to octet-stream — with the handler extracted to assets.ts and driven
  as a real Hono route over binary fixtures.

Review fixes folded in: trailing-comment directives still detected,
identity scan matches quoted literals only (no comment cry-wolf),
uppercase extensions serve.

This branch records what a lightly guided model can already do in the reference case. The findings set a factual baseline for deciding which product machinery is actually needed.

<details><summary>🏗️ Agent notes</summary>

Resolves [FE-1361](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1361): the baseline-control experiment — what does one-shot / lightly-prompted AI elicitation already achieve?

Two conditions ran against the same simulated master scheduler (Production Scheduling testbed case): bare `claude-opus-5`, and the same model armed with the seven-category v0 prompt. Everything lives under `docs/planning/process-model-elicitation/baseline/` — protocol, situation pack, v0 prompt, runner, both full transcripts, and the scored read-out (`readout.md`).

Headline findings (details and scores in the read-out, gist on the ticket):

- The bare baseline interviews far better than the positioning assumed — objectives-first, unwritten-rules probing, refusal to invent values, and an unprompted assumptions register. The differentiation story must rest on machinery, and now has evidence to rest on.
- Neither condition can end the engagement: one novel deliverable-deferral failure, one sophisticated budget-exhaustion. Completion has to be an adjudicated contract.
- The v0 prompt buys interaction shape, quantile elicitation, live category accounting, conflict-point depth, and penalty-weight co-construction; its residual gaps are the evidence-derived plugin requirements.

Also on this branch, from the review pass: the typecheck gate now covers `docs/planning/**` scripts (which surfaced and fixed a real narrowing error in the runner), and five off-by-one relative links left by the docs migration are repaired. The review's remaining repo-wide findings are filed as [FE-1399](https://linear.app/hash/issue/FE-1399).

body:
The repository needed a runnable workspace before feature work could be trusted. This branch establishes the initial package layout and checks that catch boundary and build failures early.

<details><summary>🏗️ Agent notes</summary>

FE-1388: Scaffold the Bun workspace and prove the CI smoke

The repo held planning documents and no code. This lands the package
topology of spec §12.2 with its dependency direction enforced from the
first commit rather than retrofitted later, so every later slice arrives
into a structure that already refuses the wrong import.

Packages: core (plugin SDK as its export surface, with a core/testing
subpath), binding-flue, plugin-gherkin, and a dev app owning the agent
module, the mount, and the conversation store.

The direction is enforced twice over. Bun's isolated linker gives each
package only what it declares, so plugin-gherkin cannot resolve Flue or
the binding even if someone writes the import; test/boundaries.test.ts
asserts that property still holds, alongside the declared-dependency and
source-import checks, so a hoisted node_modules could not quietly restore
every forbidden path.

Two recorded Flue constraints needed opposite treatment. A computed
agentName already fails the build loudly. A 'use agent' directive that is
not the file's first statement does NOT: the build stays green and the
module simply stops being an agent, which nothing would notice until a
conversation failed to start. That one is the load-bearing check in the
boundary suite.

Nothing here ratifies the SDK export surface. Spec §13's two-targets rule
keeps the plugin contract unfrozen until the hard target has stressed it,
so the plugin descriptor carries identity only and the ask tool fixes its
name and schema seam while its behaviour waits for FE-1389.

The product name stays provisional in one constant, and the tool prefix
derives from it — the name-fog costs one edit rather than a rename.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

FE-1388: Close the review findings — make the gates able to fail

Review found that three of the guards this ticket added could not
actually go red, which is the same failure mode as a green build that
compiled nothing.

- The CI lint step was decorative. oxlint reports its default rules at
  warning severity and exits 0 for them, so `oxlint .` passed whatever
  landed; it now runs with --deny-warnings, and a test asserts that.
- The boundary suite was never typechecked: the root tsconfig included
  every package's src and test but not the repo-root test/ directory, so
  a type error in the file that enforces the architecture shipped green.
- sourceFiles() scanned src/ only and returned [] for anything else, so a
  package laid out differently would pass every file-level invariant
  vacuously. The scan now covers the whole package directory, and a test
  asserts each package was actually scanned.

Also honest now: the dev app's / route no longer serves a page whose only
script 404s after a build. @flue/vite builds the server environment
alone, so there is no client bundle to serve; the built server says so
and vite build earns its CI place by compiling the agent module.

Smaller: REPO_ROOT resolves through fileURLToPath rather than a
percent-encoded URL.pathname; a workspace directory missing a manifest
reports that rather than crashing the suite with ENOENT; bunfig.toml pins
the isolated linker that makes the dependency direction physical; and the
four per-package tsconfigs were referenced by nothing, so they are gone
rather than left to drift.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

</details>
